content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint ORR by BICR may not capture full treatment effect",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of the study is the ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1 as determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR).",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary objective is to determine confirmed objective response with CMP-001 in combination with nivolumab. However, the study includes intratumoral injections, and RECIST v1.1 may not capture responses in injected lesions that are not target lesions. The exploratory endpoint uses itRECIST, but the primary endpoint may underestimate the treatment effect, leading to potential failure to meet the objective.",
      "fix": "Consider using a composite endpoint that includes itRECIST or iRECIST for the primary analysis, or justify the use of RECIST v1.1 with BICR for this intratumoral therapy."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for BRAF V600 mutation positive patients is overly restrictive",
      "quote": "Patients with BRAF V600 mutations who refuse a BRAF inhibitor will not be eligible.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This criterion excludes patients who may have contraindications or intolerability to BRAF inhibitors, not just those who refuse. It may limit enrollment and does not align with standard clinical practice where such patients might be eligible for immunotherapy.",
      "fix": "Allow eligibility for patients who are not candidates for BRAF inhibitor therapy due to medical reasons, not just those who refuse."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for refractory to PD-1 blockade may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "Have PD (according to RECIST v1.1) within 12 weeks of the last dose of a PD-1 blocking antibody, either as monotherapy or in combination with other agents.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.3b",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The definition of 'refractory' requires PD within 12 weeks of last dose, but it is unclear if this includes patients who had PD while on therapy or after discontinuation. This ambiguity may lead to inconsistent interpretation and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify that PD must have occurred while on therapy or within 12 weeks of the last dose, and specify whether patients who discontinued due to toxicity are included."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for measurable disease may be too restrictive",
      "quote": "One or more measurable lesions at least 1 cm in diameter that are not intended for CMP-001 injection and can be followed as target lesions per RECIST v1.1.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.4b",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring a non-injected measurable lesion of at least 1 cm may exclude patients with only small lesions or those where all lesions are suitable for injection. This could limit enrollment and may not be necessary for the study objectives.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing non-injected lesions that are measurable per RECIST v1.1 without the 1 cm minimum, or allow injected lesions to also serve as target lesions if they meet criteria."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for active autoimmune disease may be overly broad",
      "quote": "Active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years; replacement therapy is not considered a form of systemic treatment.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.2.11",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 2-year window may exclude patients with well-controlled autoimmune conditions that are unlikely to flare with immunotherapy. This could reduce enrollment and is not aligned with some other immunotherapy trials that use a shorter window or allow certain conditions.",
      "fix": "Consider shortening the window to 1 year or specifying exceptions for conditions like vitiligo, psoriasis, or thyroiditis that are typically manageable."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for adrenal insufficiency is only a note, not a protocol requirement",
      "quote": "NOTE: Subjects previously treated with a CTLA-4–blocking antibody, subjects receiving corticosteroids with daily doses > 5 mg and ≤ 10 mg of prednisone equivalent for > 2 weeks, and subjects with clinical symptoms and/or laboratory findings suggesting risk for adrenal insufficiency should undergo diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency via local laboratory.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2.6",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The note is advisory and not a mandatory safety monitoring step. Given the combination of CMP-001 and nivolumab, which can cause immune-related adrenal insufficiency, this should be a protocol-required assessment to ensure patient safety.",
      "fix": "Make the diagnostic testing for adrenal insufficiency a mandatory procedure in the protocol, with specific timing and criteria."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for prior radiation therapy may be too restrictive",
      "quote": "Received radiation therapy (or other nonsystemic therapy) within 2 weeks before first dose of study treatment on W1D1.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "A 2-week washout for radiation may be unnecessarily long for palliative radiation, which is often used in melanoma. This could delay enrollment and is not consistent with some other trials that allow a shorter interval.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing the washout to 1 week or allowing palliative radiation to non-target lesions with a shorter interval."
    },
    {
      "title": "Lack of specific safety monitoring for intratumoral injections",
      "quote": "Evaluate the safety and tolerability of CMP-001 administered by IT injection in combination with nivolumab",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.1.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify detailed safety monitoring for intratumoral injection-related adverse events, such as injection site reactions, pain, or systemic effects from local administration. This is a critical safety aspect for an IT therapy.",
      "fix": "Add specific safety assessments for injection-related AEs, including local tolerability, and define management guidelines for injection-related toxicities."
    }
  ]
}
